name: Greystar
why: Largest US apartment manager (catalog ~950,000 units); residents pay through the community's resident portal/app.

name: MAA (Mid-America Apartment Communities)
why: Major Sunbelt apartment REIT (~100,000 homes); MyMAA resident portal.

name: AvalonBay Communities (Avalon Access)
why: Large coastal apartment REIT (~90,000 homes) with its own Avalon Access resident portal.

name: Equity Residential
why: Large urban apartment REIT (~80,000 homes) with its own resident portal.

name: Camden Property Trust (MyCamden)
why: Large Sunbelt apartment REIT (~58,000 homes) with its own MyCamden portal.

name: Invitation Homes
why: Largest single-family rental landlord (~80,000+ homes); distinctive rules (AutoPay only on the 1st, no partial payments).

name: AMH (American Homes 4 Rent)
why: Second-largest single-family rental landlord (~60,000 homes).

name: Progress Residential
why: Major single-family rental landlord (~90,000 homes) with documented pay-by-phone, text-to-pay and cash options.

name: New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA)
why: Largest US public housing authority (~145,000 households); city-run online rent payment with published card fees.

name: UDR
why: Large apartment REIT (~60,000 homes) with the UDR Resident app; replaces Essex, whose public resident pages block automated reading (HTTP 429) and RentCafe login is behind a bot wall.

name: Asset Living
why: Largest US third-party apartment manager (~300,000 units); per-property resident portals, contact via the resident form/HQ line.

name: Avenue5 Residential
why: Large third-party manager (~150,000 homes in 30 states); 24/7 resident portal, Bilt rent rewards, separate former-resident billing line.

name: WinnCompanies
why: Largest US affordable/military housing manager (240,000+ residents); Resident Help Center line.

name: Bozzuto
why: Major Mid-Atlantic/Northeast manager (~95,000 homes); resident inquiry and escalation paths.

name: Morgan Properties
why: One of the largest US apartment owner-operators (~95,000 homes); RentCafe Resident Login; FAQ documents bank/card rent payments (Apple Pay and Masterpass at some communities) and rent due on the first.

name: Cortland
why: Large Sunbelt owner-operator (~85,000 homes); community-picker Resident Login and Cortland app with scheduled rent payments.

name: Bell Partners (Bell Apartment Living)
why: Large apartment manager (~65,000-70,000 homes); RentCafe Resident Login, per-community customer service.

name: Tricon Residential
why: Major single-family rental landlord (~38,000 homes) with detailed public rent-payment FAQ (Auto-Pay setup, WIPS cash, NSF limits, mail rules). Replaces Essex, whose public pages still return HTTP 429.

name: IRT Living
why: Apartment REIT (~33,000 homes) with a 24/7 portal (pay, balance, auto payments) and Flex split rent.

name: Laguna Woods Village
why: Largest US senior community association (~12,700 manors); monthly assessments with card-only online payment (3.5% fee) and form-based EZ Pay. Chosen over The Villages amenity fee (billed on the VCDD combined utility bill, a municipal-portal site) and Puerto Rico public housing (offline). Also ranked above the remaining higher-count candidates: skilled-nursing operators (Ensign, PACS) and HUD management agents bill residents through facilities, not a rent portal; Chicago Housing Authority kept for a later tier.
